title: What burlesque opera is; a light opera at the Civic Theater
summary: Hirsch tries to recall the name of a show he played at the Civic Theater, a light opera with a couple of hit songs, before a phone call interrupts.

story.theme_name: Late-career reflections: awards, legacy and life lessons
story.community_name: Hunting for old band photographs and scrapbooks

blocks.x: Burlesque opera? Mm-hmm. There was one... that I played... that it's... it's... it's not musical comedy, it's not opera, and it's not burlesque. but, uh... Now, what the hell is the name of that show? I played the show at the Civic Theater. It had popular... the song in it, Big D, Dallas, and standing on the corner watching all the girls go by. Yeah. There was two songs in there that were popular, and two songs that...
I can't... I can't remember... I saw the show... I saw the show in New York, too.
Well, I can look it up, don't worry.
I know what it is. I can find it in two seconds. But, uh... it's... let's put it this way. The soprano doesn't die in the last act.
Or the fat lady doesn't sing. Yeah. When it's over. You understand?
It's more like a light opera?
Excuse me, there's a phone call for Kurt Gerdy. That's me? Look, you can take it right there if you want to.
I can do better than that. Wait a minute. Here. Come sit down. Sit down over there.
It's all right. You can leave it there. Oh, okay.
